observations: All four photos show the same object: an old foot-treadle sewing machine mounted in a dark-red wooden cabinet/table with a cast-iron treadle base.
The machine head is cream/white metal, visibly chipped and rust-spotted in several areas (clearest in photo 1).
A brand name is embossed on the machine body, readable as 'Mercury' in photos 1 and 2.
No electric motor, power cord, or plug is visible anywhere; the cast-iron foot-treadle mechanism under the table is the only drive system shown (all photos, especially photo 2 and 3).
No accessories (bobbins, extra feet, oil can) or manual are visible in any photo.
The setting is an outdoor roadside/shop frontage with advertising banners in the background, not a dedicated showroom.
Wood veneer on the table shows wear, scuffing, and water-stain-like discoloration.

claims.evidence: Photo 1 shows chipped paint and rust spots on the machine housing; wooden table shows wear and staining.
No country-of-origin marking is legible in any photo; only the brand name 'Mercury' is visible.
No electric motor is visible in any photo; the machine is driven by a foot treadle (photos 2 and 3), so a 'motor' claim cannot apply to what is shown.

claims.claim: All accessories and the original manual
claims.evidence: No accessories, bobbins, or manual are shown in any of the four photos.

claims.claim: Never serviced because nothing ever went wrong
claims.evidence: Service history cannot be seen in photos; this is a seller statement only.

risks.risk: Mechanical condition / stitch quality unknown (does the machine actually sew a clean line?)
risks.proof: A short video of the treadle being pedaled and the needle stitching fabric.

risks.risk: Missing accessories and manual despite claim
risks.proof: A photo laid out showing bobbins, extra feet, and the manual booklet.
risks.if_unproven: priced as bare machine with table only, no accessories

risks.risk: Rust/corrosion extent on internal mechanism, not just visible housing
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the needle bar, bobbin case, and underside gears.
risks.if_unproven: priced assuming surface rust reflects similar internal wear

risks.risk: Treadle belt and pedal mechanism integrity
risks.proof: Photo/video of the treadle wheel and belt in motion.
risks.if_unproven: priced assuming belt may need replacement

proof_requests: Video of the treadle machine being pedaled and stitching a piece of fabric.
Close-up photos of accessories and the original manual, laid out together.
Close-up of any nameplate showing country of origin.
Photo of the treadle belt and underside mechanism.
response.reason: The item is clearly identifiable as an old Mercury-brand treadle sewing machine in a wooden table, with visible wear and no evidence of an electric motor, accessories, or manual as claimed, so it is priced at the worst case of a basic, unverified manual machine.
